## Appearance

Mrs. Lynde possesses a sonsy, kindly, and matronly appearance.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Again P16](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0016)_

## Personality

A capable and farseeing woman, she is a remarkably active worker in church affairs who is deeply committed to her duties. Known for being outspoken, opinionated, and a bit officious, she prides herself on speaking her mind without hesitation and is an eager judge of human nature and housekeeping. Though she can be bossy, critical, and gossipy, she remains a genuinely kindly and generous soul who is easily shocked by naughtiness. Her worldview includes a belief in foreordination and a strong skepticism toward higher education for women as well as the writing of fiction. Furthermore, she is a red-hot politician who keeps a sharp eye on local happenings and is always eager to offer advice. In addition to her social and community involvement, she possesses practical skills in sewing, dressmaking, and knitting cotton-warp quilts.

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde was raised in a household where she brought up ten children and lost two, and she had been married at eighteen. A long-standing housekeeper in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) who knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she lived as a neighbor to [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) for forty-five years without ever having a quarrel. Observing [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) leaving town dressed in his best clothes, Mrs. Lynde went to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to investigate and warned [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) about the risks of adopting an unknown child from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia). On her first meeting with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Mrs. Lynde made blunt remarks about her red hair, provoking a fierce outburst from the girl; [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) later offered a dramatic apology, which Mrs. Lynde accepted before giving her flowers. [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) frequently consulted her for practical advice, such as letting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) stay home from school when she was upset with her teacher. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) wished to gift [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a stylish dress, he enlisted Mrs. Lynde to purchase and sew the garment for her. ## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

> "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026)

> "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P8](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0008)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--rachel-lynde.md)

The relationship began with open hostility when Mrs. Lynde insulted Anne's appearance, causing [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to fly into a rage, though Mrs. Lynde accepted Anne's apology and gave her flowers. Over time, Mrs. Lynde became a trusted source of advice regarding Anne's upbringing and troubles. By the third volume, Mrs. Lynde grew into an affectionate neighbor who embraced [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and urged her to take care of her health.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), +14 more_

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Lynde and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) are longtime neighbors, tea companions, and close comrades who even travel together to a political mass meeting. Mrs. Lynde frequently visits [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to discuss local news and offer [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) counsel regarding household and child-rearing matters. Following the death of Mrs. Lynde's husband, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) invited her to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so she would not have to leave [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).

### [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/matthew-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Lynde acts as a friend and trusted neighbor to [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), though she initially expressed strong skepticism when he drove off to adopt an orphan.
